title: Diabetes emergencies in the hospital: DKA, HHS and hypoglycemia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's diabetes (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Hypoglycemic coma

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on RA, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for lethargy.
Neurological: Positive for altered mental status.
Endocrine: Positive for T2DM.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

History of Present Illness: 
(Copied Forward): Patient is an 89-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes. She was brought to the emergency department by EMS after being found unresponsive. Initial assessment revealed a state of hypoglycemi and a deep coma. 

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the intensive care unit for management of a hypoglycemic coma. Laboratory results confirmed a severe drop in blood glucose levels secondary to sulfonylurea toxicity. Treatment was initiated with immediate IV dextrose. The patient responded well to the intervention, with blood glucose levels stabilizing and consciousness returning. She remained for observation to ensure metabolic stability. She was transitioned to oral intake and met all criteria for discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Hypoglycemi
2. Coma
3. Type 2 diabetes

Discharge Medications:
1. Metformin 500mg BID
2. Glipizide 5mg daily (adjusted)

Follow-up:
Follow-up with primary care physician in 7 days.

Electronically signed, 
P. O'Brien, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes with hypoglycemia with coma: E11.641 (HCC 36).
